atoms.text: The removed predator: killing the top consumer lets the next level explode and strip the producers, so one death reorganizes a world.
The indirect effect: no one touches the plants, yet they die because a predator disappeared, so causation is distant and invisible.
The behavior shift: prey change where they feed when predators are present, so fear itself sculpts the landscape.
The overpopulation: herbivores multiply without limit and consume their own future, so prosperity becomes collapse.
The invasive top predator: a new species takes the apex role and reroutes the entire web, so the ecosystem has no immunity to a strong outsider.
The bottom-up world: nutrient supply controls everything above it, so power flows from the base rather than the top.
The subsidy: external food supports a population that the local system cannot sustain, so charity destabilizes the recipient.
The restored predator: reintroducing an apex species repairs the cascade, so the story's solution is to bring back a feared figure.
The manager who thinks they are in charge: humans remove and add species and discover the system answers in ways they did not intend, so stewardship is improvisation.
The food web as politics: each level's interests are served by controlling the one below, so ecology is a hierarchy of exploitation.
The lake experiment: adding large fish changes the plankton, so a contained world demonstrates a general law.
The collapse that looks like abundance: the middle level thrives while the base is being eaten, so success is a lagging indicator.
The predator as keystone: one species holds the architecture in place, so removing it is not a loss but a demolition.
The fishing fleet: humans hunt the apex and call the resulting shortage a natural cycle, so the story indicts management itself.
The cascade across borders: effects travel through a system with no respect for property lines, so jurisdiction cannot contain consequence.
The cascade in reverse: a small change at the bottom propagates upward through every level, so the story's lever is humble and remote.
